preserved_objections.basis: The proposed dynamic pre-charge pulse control system using wide-bandgap semiconductors is not a novel solution for mitigating lithium plating on the graphite anode, as it is based on existing research in the field of lithium-ion battery management systems (Liu et al., 2020). The use of machine learning algorithms to optimize the charging process is also not a new concept, as it has been explored in various studies on battery management systems (Zhang et al., 2019).

The candidate fails to consider the thermal management system of the electric-bus depot, which is a critical factor in preventing lithium plating on the graphite anode during fast charging. The proposed solution does not account for the potential thermal runaway that can occur during high-power charging, which can lead to lithium plating and capacity fade (Kim et al., 2018).

The candidate cites a study on fast charging methods for lithium titanate batteries (doi:10.1109/acpee56931.2023.10135597), which is not relevant to the proposed solution, as the candidate is targeting lithium-titanate-free batteries. Additionally, the study does not provide any evidence that the proposed dynamic control system can reduce lithium plating on the graphite anode.

The candidate's predicted effect of reducing lithium plating on the graphite anode by 30% and extending the battery's lifespan by 20% is not significantly different from the baseline, as the baseline is already a state-of-the-art lithium-titanate-free fast-charging battery pack. The candidate's solution does not provide any substantial improvement over the existing technology.
